title: Config Shadow Evaluation: Establishing Shadow Cohorts and Judge Consistency Metrics
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Build a reproducible shadow-evaluation pipeline that replays production-like request cohorts against proposed config/model variants and produces judge-consistency and calibration metrics tied to each config toggle. This ticket defines the rubric, sampling strategy, judge-ensemble protocol, and acceptance signals we will use to gate config rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow cohorts can be generated from historical traffic for three workload classes (short prompts, long-form, instruction-following) and replayed deterministically
Automated LLM-judge ensemble runs produce per-cohort agreement, aggregated calibration error (ECE), and delta-signals aligned with manual juried adjudication within ±3%
A config-change dashboard displays regression flags for: judge-agreement drop, calibration drift, and cohort-specific sensitivity with clear suggested mitigation actions
Integration hooks to rollout engine so that a regression flag can mark a canary rollout as blocked or trigger auto-fallback
tasks: Define shadow cohort selection rules and synthetic-control cohorts
Design judge rubric with discrete label taxonomy and confidence buckets
Implement LLM-judge ensemble runner in eval-harness (support streaming judge outputs and vote aggregation)
Compute calibration metrics (ECE, Brier, reliability curves) and judge agreement (pairwise kappa and plurality rate)
Instrument dashboard panels and alerting thresholds for automated gating
Run initial smoke tests on two recent config changes and compare to historical juried adjudication
comments: 2026-02-12 Priya Nair: Kickoff - scoped initial MVP to shadow-eval for text-generation configs (batching, quantization profile, kernel-choice). Attached proposed rubric draft.

2026-02-16 Evan Liu: Engineering spike started. Built baseline harness to replay archived requests into staging. Found that KV-cache interactions need instrumentation to produce consistent prefixes for replay.

2026-02-20 Rafael Ortiz (Review): Suggested we separate judge prompts for style vs. correctness to avoid conflating calibration signals. Also recommended 200 sample juried checks per cohort for statistical power.
2026-02-24 Design review (Maya Chen): Added UI mocks for per-config delta charts and color-coded gating indicators. Mock link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Ui_mock_design

2026-02-26 Evan Liu: Hooked up LLM-judge ensemble (3 models: judge-small, judge-med, judge-large) and implemented plurality voting + confidence averaging. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/642

2026-02-28 Priya Nair: Ran smoke on config toggle 'enable-prefix-caching-v2' against 5k historical requests. Early signal: judge agreement dropped 6% in long-form cohort; calibration ECE increased from 0.12 to 0.18. Logged as preliminary regression.

2026-03-01 PM feedback: Need to quantify false-positive rate vs juried adjudication. Action: run juried sample of 500 cases across cohorts and compare disagreement cases for root cause analysis. Assigned to Evan.
notes: Design decisions: Use juried adjudication as ground truth for calibration alignment checks but rely on LLM-judge ensemble for continuous, high-volume monitoring
Sampling: Stratify by customer tier and route to detect config-sensitive regressions that affect high-commit customers first
Metrics: Produce both relative deltas and absolute thresholds to avoid flagging noise for low-volume cohorts
Rollback plan: If threshold exceeded during canary, automatically pause rollout and switch traffic to previous model variant; notify on-call SRE and product owner
Risks: LLM-judge bias toward scale/verbosity; banking too heavily on single judge model increases false-positive regressions. We'll mitigate via ensemble diversity and juried spot checks
